title: 2023 discretionary grant envelopes recommended
subtitle: Committee also heard REEP Green Solutions' impact report and asked for inflation to be considered in 2024 grants.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Regional Council approve the 2023 discretionary grant program envelopes, totalling $5,603,820 {{vote:m1}}. Staff said the amounts match what was approved in the February 22, 2023 budget and are unchanged from 2022. The report was brought forward so everyone has a clear picture of each envelope as the application and reporting process begins.

The committee also directed staff to include inflationary considerations for grant funding in the 2024 budget. For residents, this means community organizations that rely on regional grants may see funding that keeps pace with rising costs, though nothing has been decided for 2024.

Earlier, the committee heard a delegation from REEP Green Solutions on its impact report, covering home energy evaluations, community programs, a planned tree nursery and work on energy poverty. A councillor also recognized regional parking enforcement staff for collaborating on community safety. The committee received the tracking list for information. Its next meeting is April 4, 2023.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the 2023 grant program envelopes totalling $5,603,820, as set out in report COR-ADM-23-002.

debate: One councillor asked why the grant envelopes needed approval again when the budget had approved them two weeks earlier. Staff said the report was brought forward out of caution, so everyone has a common understanding of each envelope, and that the amounts are unchanged from 2022.
Another councillor asked that grant funding rise by at least the rate of inflation in next year's budget, and wanted the item flagged so it isn't lost in the large budget document.

Councillors questioned REEP delegates about working with neighbourhood associations and utilities. Delegates described project-based work such as de-paving, and continuing talks with local utilities on funding opportunities.

On the planned tree nursery, a councillor asked whether existing nurseries collaborate. Delegates said this is the first real chance to do so, with the Woolwich nursery as a partner and outreach to other municipalities.
On equity, a delegate said a consultant's research found that home energy loans can be a burden for lower-income households, and that default rates are not a good measure of a program's success.
